current_proposal.summary: Fix payment timeouts by applying the documented RetryPolicy change to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50, retrying only timeouts and returning upstream errors immediately, with no change to the per-request timeout and no added Idempotency-Key handling.
plan_steps: Set the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 total attempts with jitter_ms = 50, changing it from the default max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0.
Keep retry scope timeout-only: retry only SendError::Timeout up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts and return upstream errors, including HTTP 502, 503, and 504 responses, at once without a retry.
Do not change the per-request timeout: remove the proposed 5-second timeout increase, for which no documented maximum limit was retrieved.
Do not add or rely on Idempotency-Key handling, for which no documented constraint was retrieved.
Verify that the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts passes with max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50, and monitor timeout and retry rates to detect retry bursts.

claims.statement: The 2026-09 payments review decision requires fixing payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50, and raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.

assumptions: Future payment-gateway load and latency will be broadly similar to the conditions under which the intermittent timeouts were observed, so retrying transient timeouts is expected to reduce user-visible timeouts. No stored record can settle future load or latency.
uncertainties: Whether upstream payment-gateway capacity will remain sufficient under future transaction volumes cannot be settled by any stored record.
Whether this RetryPolicy change alone will be sufficient during future peak traffic spikes cannot be settled by any stored record.

task.title: Fix payment client timeouts
task.description: Payment requests intermittently time out under load. Propose a safe fix consistent with the existing retry constraints.

proposal.summary: Increase the payment client timeout conservatively to 5 seconds, preserve the existing retry limits and idempotency protections, retry only transient failures with backoff and jitter, and improve connection reuse and observability.
plan_steps: Raise the payment client per-request timeout to 5 seconds per attempt while keeping the existing retry cap unchanged.
Keep at most 3 total attempts per payment request: 1 initial attempt plus up to 2 retries.
Retry only timeouts and HTTP 502, 503, or 504 responses; do not retry HTTP 4xx responses or any failure after a definitive payment result.
On every retry, reuse the same Idempotency-Key as the original payment request; do not retry a payment request that lacks an idempotency key.
Use exponential backoff with jitter between retries, starting at 250 milliseconds and doubling after each retry.
Enable HTTP keep-alive and connection reuse for the payment client to reduce connection-setup delays under load.
Add metrics and alerting for per-attempt timeout rate, retry rate, and gateway response time, without changing payment business logic or request payloads.

claims.statement: A 5-second per-request payment-client timeout is within the project's documented maximum timeout limit, and keeping at most 3 total attempts with retries only on timeouts and HTTP 502, 503, or 504, reusing the same idempotency key and using exponential backoff with jitter, is consistent with the project's documented payment retry constraints.

assumptions: Future payment-gateway load and latency will be broadly similar to the load under which the intermittent timeouts were observed, so a 5-second per-attempt timeout is expected to reduce timeout frequency. No stored record can settle future load or latency.
Enabling HTTP keep-alive and connection reuse is expected to reduce connection-setup queueing under load. The magnitude of this effect cannot be settled by a stored record.
uncertainties: Whether a 5-second timeout will cover future gateway p99 latency during peak traffic spikes cannot be settled by any stored record.
Whether upstream payment-gateway capacity will remain sufficient under future transaction volumes cannot be settled by any stored record.

Do not change the per-request timeout: remove the proposed 5-second timeout increase, for which no documented maximum limit was retrieved.
Do not add or rely on Idempotency-Key handling, for which no documented constraint was retrieved.
Verify that the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts passes with max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50, and monitor timeout and retry rates to detect retry bursts.

claims.statement: The 2026-09 payments review decision requires fixing payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50, and raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.

assessment.note: Record 328114099256634798832222840773545327795 directly states the 2026-09 decision to set max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 and prohibits raising the cap above 3.

assumptions: Future payment-gateway load and latency will be broadly similar to the conditions under which the intermittent timeouts were observed, so retrying transient timeouts is expected to reduce user-visible timeouts. No stored record can settle future load or latency.
uncertainties: Whether upstream payment-gateway capacity will remain sufficient under future transaction volumes cannot be settled by any stored record.
Whether this RetryPolicy change alone will be sufficient during future peak traffic spikes cannot be settled by any stored record.

revisions.summary: Fix payment timeouts by applying the documented RetryPolicy change to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50, retrying only timeouts and returning upstream errors immediately, with no change to the per-request timeout and no added Idempotency-Key handling.

chain.note: This run's events form a complete hash chain from genesis on their own: recomputing every record's hash and link from them alone verifies the run. head_hash is the hash of its last event. The chain is unsigned SHA-256. A successful check shows that the records received are internally consistent; it detects a change only against a hash obtained earlier, such as this receipt's head_hash or a published manifest. It cannot detect a run rewritten and re-hashed, a truncated tail or a deleted run, and it says nothing about whether the content is true.

receipt.proof_limitations: A proof marked valid means that Hyphae's verifier re-executed the request the proof sealed against its witness and accepted it at the anchor it was given (the pinned anchor wherever one is configured, always for the public snapshot). It covers the whole result of that request (for the sealed snapshot, the complete record list of the snapshot's project at that anchor), never a claim, even when the request's query is a claim's text, and a record's text is not byte-compared with the proof. A simulated proof checks nothing. Proofs do not establish that the content is true, relevant, or complete, or that a model reasoned from it.
